The insight

Reading a script predicts almost nothing. Watching might.

Scoring script text explains under 2% of how films perform (ρ = 0.135 · 9,901 titles · founder’s corpus). Audiences don’t read premises. They watch them. AI video makes any premise watchable, so the audience read can move from the end of the chain to the start.

The marketplace · you were just one of three sides

Three sides. One thing changes hands.

Now After the proof Later

Writers & production companies

GiveOne script, non-exclusive and revocable. You approve every beat and frame. Production companies: a slate, privately, under NDA.
Get
  • An instant narrative read of your script. Free. Now
  • A sell kit from your own script: one-sheet, written and visual treatments, pitch deck, concept trailer. After the proof
  • A signed Demand Certificate. Evidence, not packaging. After the proof
  • Routes we intend to open: Sundance labs, AFI, TIFF, Cannes Marché, SXSW, Nicholl partners, Frontières, BloodList. Targets. No agreements yet. Later
Keep100% of rights and proceeds. Private by default. We never represent you, and can’t promise it gets made.

Audiences

GiveFive minutes a night and honest choices. Never money.
Get
  • Watch. Four face-offs a night: short, new, nothing you have seen. Later
  • A say. Your choices reach the people who greenlight, and we publish what happened next. Later
  • Create. Deal premise cards, see a what-if teaser, and a writer can adopt it. Earned, never bought. Later
EarnTastemaker score: how early you were on what got made. Private, scored on outcomes. First looks, thanks credits, screenings. Never cash.

Industry

GiveA fee per concept, a slate under NDA, and what you decided afterwards.
Get
  • Audience demand by genre, demo and territory, with an error bar. First panels US and UK. After the proof
  • A five-surface profile: box office first, then licensing, linear, streaming, social. Later
  • Evidence for the finance pack and a demand case for originals. After the proof
  • A launch audience that already chose the concept. Later
KeepYour reads stay private. The back-test result before it is published. A founding price.

The prediction engine · why this compounds, and why us

Anyone can render a trailer. We keep score.

01Resolve

12.96M certified rows. A 220K-title pool. Guards rejected 25.6% of candidate matches as wrong; a naive join would have trained on them. Now

02Decode real · 43-title pilot

Each script’s narrative DNA, decoded on upload. This matrix is quality control: features that move together get merged. Text alone explains under 2% of outcomes. We measured it, and published it.

        Appendix 2

        Hard questions

        Does trailer reaction predict outcomes?We don’t know yet. That is exactly what gate zero tests, blind and pre-registered, and the result is published pass or fail.
        Aren’t you measuring the render, not the script?Every concept goes through one pipeline, one length, several takes. We report between-render variance and publish an index only where premise variance exceeds it.
        The back-test only uses films that got made.Yes. Range is restricted, so the observed correlation understates the deployed one. We say so in the pre-registration, and we don’t use it to rescue a fail.
        Why won’t a studio or a streamer build this?They can build the renderer. They can’t build a cross-buyer ledger, because nobody shares drafts with a competitor. Closest today: simulated-audience tools, which are not real behaviour.
        Greenlights are driven by packaging, not concept.For tentpoles, yes. In horror and low-budget genre the concept leads, which is why we start there. This is a filter and a cover memo, not a greenlight machine.
        What if it fails?We publish the failure, having spent about $18K to learn it. What remains is a feature of the founder’s data platform, not a company.
        Appendix 3 · for counsel to confirm

        Rights and AI

        The trailer is a test stimulus.It is never released as a film and never the product. Assume raw AI output is not copyrightable (USCO Part 2, Jan 2025; Thaler cert denied, Mar 2026). The data is the asset.
        Writers.Upload-time licence: non-exclusive, revocable, derivative marketing materials only. Writer warrants chain of title and no WGA-contracted material. No training use without a separate opt-in.
        Faces and voices.Synthetic only. No real-actor likeness, no fan-casting. Similarity check before anything is shown. Any buyer who is a guild signatory inherits the 2026 SAG-AFTRA terms.
        Buyers.Mutual NDA and a data addendum. Closed panel under click-through NDA, watermarked, never near the open market, deleted on request.
        Model providers.Commercial-use terms are read before any customer-facing render, and every model sits behind an adapter so it can be swapped. Studios have already challenged one video-model vendor over training data.
        Audiences.Panelists are paid or entertained. Nothing is sold to them and nothing promises a return. No pledges, tokens or equity in this plan.
